answer_1.quote: We experiment on machine translation (MT), text summarization (SUM), and data-to-text (D2T), and show that BARTScore++ consistently and significantly improves the performance of vanilla BARTScore...
answer_1.outputs: generated translations, generated summaries, data-to-text utterances

answer_2.quote: We compare our method with several commonly used baseline metrics for evaluating text generation, including BLEU, BERTScore, MoverScore and PRISM. For MT tasks, we also consider supervised metrics that leverage human judgments to train, including COMET and BLEURT.

answer_3.quote: Besides taking BARTScore as the testbed ... we also show the universality in the recently advanced language model ChatGPT by designing an error-analysis-based prompt.

answer_4.quote: MQM is an error-based human evaluation framework ... annotators are asked to identify all errors in a sentence and categorize them into Major and Minor levels indicating their severities.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators identify errors in the hypothesis and assign them to Major (explicit) or Minor (implicit) categories; weighted sum of errors yields the MQM score.
